question: Why is it so important to ask about a client's last menstrual period before starting birth control?

options.A: To check if the client has an active sexually transmitted infection
options.B: To calculate the exact date of menopause the client will experience
options.C: To reasonably rule out an existing, early pregnancy before starting birth control
options.D: To determine how many children the client has delivered in the past

explanation: Spot on! We always want to be sure a client isn't already pregnant before starting certain contraceptives to keep both her and the early pregnancy safe.

question: What is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane called?

options.A: Active transport
options.B: Pinocytosis
options.C: Simple diffusion
options.D: Osmosis

explanation: Osmosis is the specific term for the passive movement of water molecules across a membrane from an area of lower solute concentration to higher solute concentration. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why do frontline nurses sometimes resist monitoring and quality controls from their managers?

options.A: They prefer spending their entire shift filling out paper incident logs
options.B: They believe hospital administrators want patient care standards to be low
options.C: They may view the controls as micromanagement and a sign of mistrust
options.D: They are legally forbidden from participating in quality improvement

explanation: If monitoring isn't explained well, staff can feel spied on rather than supported, leading to pushback against helpful safety checks.

question: Which of these methods is NOT a reliable way to make water safe from amoebic cysts?

options.A: Boiling the water vigorously for at least one minute
options.B: Allowing the water to settle in a dark container for an hour
options.C: Using certified chemical disinfection tablets
options.D: Filtering the water through a fine membrane filter

explanation: You got it! Letting water settle just drops heavy dirt—it doesn't kill microscopic cysts. Always boil, filter, or treat chemically!

question: What is the standard temperature inside a clinical incubator for growing human pathogens?

options.A: 80 to 90 degrees Celsius
options.B: 35 to 37 degrees Celsius
options.C: 10 to 15 degrees Celsius
options.D: 50 to 60 degrees Celsius

explanation: Think about normal body temperature! Since these germs live inside human hosts, the incubator is set right around 37°C to make them feel right at home.

question: Why did nurse leaders in the 1970s feel the need to build their own unique nursing theories?

options.A: To replace all medical textbooks with nursing journals
options.B: To prove that nurses were more important than physicians in hospitals
options.C: To better explain and guide the unique aspects of professional nursing care
options.D: To satisfy strict government tax requirements for universities

explanation: Think of it this way: borrowed theories couldn't fully capture what makes nursing special. Leaders needed original frameworks to truly guide everyday clinical practice.

question: As a community nurse, you teach villagers to clear stagnant water around their homes to stop mosquitoes. Which part of the epidemiological triangle are you targeting?

options.A: The human host
options.B: The clinical symptoms
options.C: The environment
options.D: The infectious agent

explanation: Exactly! Clearing stagnant water changes the external environment to take away breeding sites for the mosquitoes.

question: Why might a patient with very low white blood cells (neutropenia) NOT show classic signs of infection like pus?

options.A: They lack enough white blood cells to mount an inflammatory response
options.B: Their body temperature stays too low to support white blood cell activity
options.C: Their platelets bind up all the available immune cells
options.D: Their blood vessels are too constricted to allow fluid movement

explanation: Pus is basically a pile of used white blood cells that fought an infection. If a patient doesn't have enough white blood cells to begin with, infections can sneak in quietly—often with just a fever as the only clue!

question: A patient is brought in bleeding heavily from a leg wound and gasping for air. Following the ABCDE approach, what should you address first?

options.A: Ask the patient for their home address and phone number
options.B: Ensure a patent airway and check breathing
options.C: Clean the leg wound with antiseptic solution
options.D: Document the exact time of the injury in the chart

explanation: Airway and breathing always come first in the ABCDE sequence—even before stopping severe bleeding in circulation! Think A-B-C.

question: Why is keeping your midwifery kit well-organized and checked regularly so important?

options.A: It makes expired tools magically renew themselves
options.B: It keeps the outside bag looking very professional and neat
options.C: It is a strict rule just to pass hospital uniform inspections
options.D: It stops you from wasting precious time searching for tools during an emergency delivery

explanation: When a baby is in a hurry to arrive, every second counts! Knowing exactly where everything is keeps you calm and in control.

question: Which medical protection is mandatory for all nursing students and staff before starting clinical duties?

options.A: Tetanus booster every month
options.B: Daily antimalarial medication
options.C: Prophylactic antiretroviral therapy
options.D: Hepatitis B vaccination

explanation: Correct! The Hepatitis B vaccine protects you against one of the most common bloodborne hazards in the hospital. Safety first!

question: Why is encapsulation often used specifically for pharmaceutical waste?

options.A: To turn expired tablets into sweet-tasting liquid syrups
options.B: To immobilize chemical drugs and prevent them from entering water supplies
options.C: To bleach colored medicine bottles so they can be recycled
options.D: To make heavy metal containers easier to burn in an incinerator

explanation: Encapsulation binds drugs in a solid matrix like cement, stopping them from dissolving and leaching into soil and groundwater. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h5)

question: What is the main goal of the health team concept in patient care?

options.A: To deliver the highest quality of care through shared work
options.B: To ensure doctors make all final decisions independently
options.C: To lower the overall financial cost of running a clinic
options.D: To reduce the number of hospital staff on duty daily

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare is a team sport. By working together, different professionals combine their skills to give patients the absolute best care possible.

question: What should you do if you are unsure whether a sterile package is still clean?

options.A: Use the item quickly before anyone notices the error
options.B: Treat the item as contaminated and get a new one
options.C: Ask another nurse to guess if the item is still safe
options.D: Wipe the outside package with alcohol and use it anyway

explanation: Safety first! In nursing, if there is ever any doubt about an item's sterility, we assume it's contaminated and grab a fresh one. Never gamble with a patient's safety.

question: What is a key safety requirement for storing cleaning chemicals in a day care centre?

options.A: Storing them securely out of reach of children
options.B: Placing them next to food preparation counters
options.C: Keeping them unlocked on low shelves for easy access
options.D: Mixing them with drinking water for cleaning

explanation: Toxic chemicals must always be stored securely away from children to prevent accidental poisoning or chemical burns. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of competency-based training over normal classroom lectures for PAC nurses?

options.A: It allows the training course to be completed in under one hour
options.B: It ensures learners prove practical clinical skill before treating patients
options.C: It focuses solely on reading policy documents and guidelines
options.D: It completely removes the need for any clinical supervisors

explanation: Competency-based learning is all about hands-on practice and actually mastering the skill, so you feel confident stepping into the clinical ward.

question: Why is it so important to include informal sector workers in Nigerian health insurance schemes?

options.A: It stops people from visiting traditional healers
options.B: It ensures that doctors no longer have to work in rural areas
options.C: It broadens the financial base and pools risk more effectively
options.D: It reduces the total population requiring medical care

explanation: Since a huge portion of Nigeria's workforce is in the informal sector, including them is the key to achieving true universal health coverage for everyone!

question: Which symptom is a major warning sign of botulism poisoning from Clostridium botulinum?

options.A: Severe joint swelling and stiffness
options.B: High fever and immediate skin rashes
options.C: Rapid hair loss within twenty-four hours
options.D: Muscle paralysis affecting the nervous system

explanation: Clostridium botulinum makes a potent neurotoxin that blocks nerve signals, leading to muscle weakness and paralysis. Safety first with canned and preserved foods!

question: Why do we need different sectors—like health, law enforcement, and social services—to work together when managing violence cases?

options.A: Because police officers must approve all nursing care plans
options.B: Because survivors need medical, legal, social, and psychological support
options.C: Because hospital nurses have the legal power to arrest criminals
options.D: Because social workers are the only ones allowed to treat physical injuries

explanation: Spot on! No single profession can fix every problem a violence survivor faces. Teamwork across health, law, and social services is essential.

question: A clinic nurse tests a urine sample from a 32-week pregnant woman and finds protein in it. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Gestational hypertension with pre-eclampsia
options.B: Normal physiological kidney adaptation
options.C: Severe iron-deficiency anemia
options.D: Dietary sugar overload from lunch

explanation: Protein in the urine combined with high blood pressure later in pregnancy is a classic warning sign of pre-eclampsia that needs immediate attention.

question: What is 'hungry bone syndrome', which can happen right after a parathyroidectomy?

options.A: Remodeled bones rapidly take up calcium and phosphate to rebuild their structure.
options.B: The surgical incision causes temporary starvation and loss of appetite.
options.C: The remaining parathyroid glands instantly shut down all hormone production.
options.D: The kidneys suddenly stop filtering waste products from the bloodstream.

explanation: Once high PTH is suddenly removed, starved bones eagerly soak up calcium from the blood to rebuild themselves, causing blood calcium to drop fast!

question: Why is buying healthcare different from buying regular items like shoes or phones?

options.A: The price of medical care never changes based on economic factors
options.B: Patients can easily treat themselves without professional assistance
options.C: Healthcare items are always distributed by governments for free
options.D: People demand healthcare because they want health, not because it is a source of pleasure

explanation: Nobody wakes up wishing to visit the hospital for fun! We seek care simply to get our health back and function well. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why can it cause trouble if an NGO runs a health project without involving local health authorities?

options.A: The health program may collapse when donor funding ends
options.B: Local nurses will refuse to treat any sick patients
options.C: The government will fine the community health workers
options.D: The clinic will automatically become a profit-making business

explanation: You got it! Without government ties and local teamwork, projects usually fall apart the moment foreign funders leave. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h4)

question: During a shift handover, which drug history detail is most critical to share?

options.A: The decorative color of the pill organizer brought from home
options.B: The brand name of the multivitamin taken once last year
options.C: Active high-risk medications like blood thinners and recent changes
options.D: The specific name of the retail pharmacy where drugs are bought

explanation: High-risk drugs require immediate team awareness during handovers to prevent severe adverse events. Excellent clinical judgment!

question: What is a mandatory requirement for any injectable (parenteral) drug preparation?

options.A: It must contain a high concentration of added sugar
options.B: It must be mixed with thick oil to slow down absorption
options.C: It must be completely sterile and free from pyrogens
options.D: It must have a strong, pleasant artificial fruit flavour

explanation: Injectable drugs bypass your patient's natural digestive defenses, so they must be completely sterile to prevent severe infections and dangerous fevers.

question: What is the main job of a receptor in a reflex pathway?

options.A: Contraction of skeletal muscle fibers
options.B: Releasing hormones directly into the bloodstream
options.C: Converting physical stimuli into electrical nerve signals
options.D: Processing complex thoughts in the cerebral cortex

explanation: Receptors act like translators, changing physical stuff like heat or touch into the electrical language that nerves can understand.

question: What turns a bunch of people living close together into a real, active community?

options.A: Active social interaction and communication among members
options.B: Having a large modern hospital in the center
options.C: Government registration of all adult residents
options.D: The presence of paved roads and electricity

explanation: It's all about communication! Neighbors become a true community when they talk, interact, and relate to one another.

question: What is the main job of the chairperson during a professional meeting?

options.A: Serving refreshments to all invited attendees
options.B: Guiding discussion and keeping the team on the agenda
options.C: Taking over patient care duties while staff are away
options.D: Writing down every single word spoken by participants

explanation: The chairperson leads the session, manages time, and ensures the group sticks to the planned topics.

question: What is a vital nursing duty once a patient is physically stable after an intentional overdose?

options.A: Scolding the patient to prevent them from trying it again
options.B: Restricting all family members from visiting the bedside
options.C: Discharging the patient immediately without further delay
options.D: Arranging a psychiatric evaluation and providing a safe space

explanation: Holistic nursing means caring for the mind too! Intentional overdoses call for compassionate mental health support and a safe, non-judgmental environment.

question: Why is effective nutrition counselling more than just handing a patient a printed diet sheet?

options.A: It requires understanding the patient's daily life and financial limits.
options.B: Patients in rural communities usually cannot read printed materials.
options.C: Doctors are the only ones legally allowed to explain diet sheets.
options.D: Printed sheets are too expensive to produce in local clinics.

explanation: Real dietary guidance must fit a patient's actual living conditions, budget, and access to local food markets rather than being a generic list. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h1)

question: Why do vaguely worded living wills cause problems for the healthcare team?

options.A: Because nurses are not legally allowed to read handwritten documents
options.B: Because insurance companies refuse to pay for vague medical forms
options.C: Because hospitals require notarized stamps on every single page
options.D: Because terms like 'heroic measures' can mean different things to different people

explanation: Vague phrases create ambiguity, leaving nurses and physicians unsure of whether the patient intended to refuse specific interventions like intubation or IV fluids. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is the typical timeframe covered by a tactical plan?

options.A: One to three years
options.B: One to seven days
options.C: A few hours
options.D: Ten to twenty years

explanation: Tactical plans are medium-term guides that usually span a period of one to three years. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the main job of GABA in the central nervous system?

options.A: It builds strong protective membranes around nerve cells
options.B: It speeds up heart rate during emergency physical stress
options.C: It acts as the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter to calm brain activity
options.D: It carries oxygen directly to neurons in the frontal lobe

explanation: GABA is basically the brain's natural calming chemical or 'brake pedal'. It slows down nerve signals so the brain doesn't get overloaded with too much electrical excitement.

question: What do we call the layer of a membrane that is stuck directly onto the surface of an organ?

options.A: parietal layer
options.B: visceral layer
options.C: mucosal layer
options.D: fibrous layer

explanation: Remember: 'visceral' relates to the internal organs themselves, while 'parietal' lines the outer wall of the cavity.

question: What does a low p-value (less than 0.05) usually let a researcher do?

options.A: Reject the null hypothesis
options.B: Change the independent variable
options.C: Eliminate all confounding factors
options.D: Ignore ethical review boards

explanation: A low p-value means your findings are statistically significant and unlikely to just be a stroke of luck!

question: What is a major sign of a high bowel blockage like a duodenal obstruction?

options.A: Inability to pass flatus
options.B: Bright red rectal bleeding
options.C: Frequent projectile vomiting
options.D: Watery diarrhea with mucus

explanation: Spot on! When the upper digestive tract is blocked, food and fluids have nowhere to go but back up, leading to frequent vomiting of stomach contents.

question: Which nutrient class serves as the body's most rapid and preferred energy source?

options.A: Vitamins
options.B: Carbohydrates
options.C: Minerals
options.D: Proteins

explanation: Carbohydrates break down quickly into glucose, which is the body and brain's favorite fuel for immediate energy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h2)

question: Why must you always wash a dirty instrument thoroughly before applying a liquid chemical disinfectant?

options.A: Physical friction is the only proven method capable of killing bacterial endospores
options.B: Organic matter like blood and mucus can block the disinfectant from reaching the microbes
options.C: Washing instruments with soap prevents the metal from rusting during the chemical soak
options.D: Cleaning chemicals neutralize the toxic residue left behind by previous sterilisation cycles

explanation: Think of dried blood or body fluids as a shield! If you don't wash them off first, the germs stay hidden and safe from your disinfectant.

question: What term do qualitative researchers use instead of traditional statistical terms like validity and reliability?

options.A: Trustworthiness
options.B: Numeric accuracy
options.C: Precision testing
options.D: Generalizability

explanation: Well done! Because qualitative work deals with stories and feelings rather than numbers, we check its quality by looking at its 'trustworthiness'.

question: A patient on regular drugs mentions starting a strong herbal supplement to sleep better. As a nurse, what is your main concern?

options.A: The herb may interact with liver enzymes and alter the prescription drug level
options.B: The patient will instantly stop taking all of their prescribed medications
options.C: The patient is violating strict hospital dietary policies
options.D: The hospital will charge extra fees for documenting natural remedies

explanation: Spot on! Herbs have active chemicals that can mess with how the body processes prescribed drugs, leading to dangerous levels in the system.

question: What is the primary hormonal job of the corpus luteum during the second half of the cycle?

options.A: Lowering body temperature to prevent fevers
options.B: Producing large amounts of follicle-stimulating hormone
options.C: Triggering the immediate shedding of the uterine wall
options.D: Secreting high levels of progesterone to maintain the womb lining

explanation: Progesterone released by the corpus luteum prepares and maintains the endometrium for a possible pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why should you clean a wound surface with sterile saline before taking a swab for culture?

options.A: To dissolve the stitches holding the wound edges together
options.B: To completely sterilize the interior of the wound
options.C: To numb the local pain receptors in the damaged tissue
options.D: To remove surface contaminants and dead skin cells

explanation: Wiping away surface debris ensures you are culturing the actual infection deep down, rather than just the dust and dead cells on top.

question: What is the main focus of a servant leader in nursing?

options.A: Prioritizing the growth and well-being of the healthcare team
options.B: Strictly punishing staff who make minor documentation errors
options.C: Avoiding all interaction with junior nursing personnel
options.D: Maintaining absolute control over all hospital financial budgets

explanation: A servant leader puts the team first. By making sure nurses are supported and well-cared for, patient care naturally becomes top-notch!

question: What should a nurse watch closest right after a patient gets an intracardiac injection?

options.A: Urine output using a bedside commode
options.B: Bowel sounds and abdominal softness
options.C: Cardiac rhythm and vital signs
options.D: Range of motion in the upper arms

explanation: You've got this! Because the heart muscle was just punctured, tracking heart rhythm and blood pressure helps catch dangerous complications right away.

question: In rehabilitation terms, how is a 'handicap' different from an 'impairment'?

options.A: An impairment is always caused by poverty
options.B: An impairment cannot be treated by nurses
options.C: A handicap is the social disadvantage resulting from a disability
options.D: A handicap refers strictly to internal organ failure

explanation: Think of an impairment as the physical body change, while a handicap is how that change creates hurdles in everyday social roles and activities. Keep pushing forward!

question: A pregnant woman comes to the clinic with her husband who actively asks about emergency transport plans. How should the nurse view this behavior?

options.A: As a positive sign of male involvement in maternal health
options.B: As an unnecessary intrusion into clinical matters
options.C: As proof that the woman cannot care for herself
options.D: As a violation of hospital privacy policies

explanation: Planning for emergency transport with a partner shows strong male involvement which protects maternal and newborn health. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h3)

question: Why are the testes located outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To produce testosterone for secondary sex traits
options.B: To store mature sperm cells before ejaculation
options.C: To keep the testes cooler than core body temperature
options.D: To secrete fluid that forms the bulk of semen

explanation: You've got this! Sperm production works best at a slightly lower temperature than our normal body heat. That is why nature designed the scrotum to hang outside the body to keep the testes nice and cool.

question: Why is it important to pre-test IEC materials with a small group before launching a full campaign?

options.A: To prove to hospital management that the nurse has finished the artwork
options.B: To check if the messages are clear, culturally acceptable, and easily understood
options.C: To ensure that the printing press company makes a good profit
options.D: To satisfy legal requirements for copyright registration

explanation: Pre-testing helps catch confusing words, offensive images, or misunderstood concepts before spending money on mass production. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h6)

question: Which of these factors generally improves the long-term outlook for a child with a behaviour disorder?

options.A: Timely and consistent therapeutic intervention
options.B: Waiting until adulthood for natural maturity
options.C: Avoiding all contact with mental health professionals
options.D: Changing schools every single year

explanation: Early, structured support from healthcare providers and family gives the child much better coping skills for a bright future!

question: Why is integrating family planning into primary healthcare centers important?

options.A: It removes the need for community health education programs.
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to work in large hospitals.
options.C: It ensures that even rural and remote communities can access services.
options.D: It makes contraceptive services exclusively available to the wealthy.

explanation: Primary health centers are right in the communities. Bringing family planning there means even folks in remote villages can easily get the care and advice they need.

question: Where is the best place to set up a sharps disposal container in a patient care area?

options.A: On the floor underneath the nurse's station desk
options.B: Inside the central facility storage warehouse
options.C: Inside the clean utility supply cupboard
options.D: As close as possible to where the injection is given

explanation: Spot on! Keeping sharps bins right at the point of use means you never have to walk across the room carrying an exposed needle. Safety first! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h8)

question: What is the big danger of giving strong pain meds (opioids) right before the baby is born?

options.A: Permanent cessation of uterine contractions
options.B: Neonatal respiratory depression
options.C: Immediate cervical closure
options.D: Severe maternal hypertension

explanation: If opioids cross the placenta right before birth, they can make it hard for the newborn to take its first good breath.

question: Which action shows proper infection control when collecting a specimen?

options.A: Recapping used needles using both hands to prevent spills
options.B: Using clean gloves and performing hand hygiene before and after
options.C: Wiping the specimen container exterior with bare hands
options.D: Storing open specimen tubes on the patient's bed sheets

explanation: Hand hygiene and gloves protect both you and your patient from spreading germs. Always clean your hands and glove up!

question: Which of these details is NOT necessary to record when documenting a syringe driver setup?

options.A: The batch number of the administered drug
options.B: The patient's favorite television program
options.C: The exact location of the insertion site
options.D: The specific infusion rate set on the pump

explanation: Too easy! While knowing their favorite show is nice for conversation, it has no place in official medication documentation.

question: How is nursing counselling different from a standard health interview?

options.A: Counselling focuses on emotional support and coping
options.B: Counselling relies exclusively on closed-ended questions
options.C: Counselling replaces all physical health assessments
options.D: Counselling is only performed by hospital chaplains

explanation: Great thinking! While an interview gathers facts, counselling helps patients process feelings and handle health challenges.

question: Which scrotal condition feels like a 'bag of worms' when a nurse feels the area during an exam?

options.A: Varicocele
options.B: Epididymitis
options.C: Hydrocele
options.D: Orchitis

explanation: A varicocele happens when veins in the scrotum become swollen and twisted, giving them that classic, bumpy 'bag of worms' feel.

question: A nurse finds a 5-year-old child with sudden, floppy weakness in both legs. What is the best immediate nursing response?

options.A: Advise the family to stay indoors and avoid all local clinic visits
options.B: Report the case as an AFP emergency and collect stool samples
options.C: Prescribe broad-spectrum oral antibiotics for home management
options.D: Reassure the parents that normal muscle tone will return in a day

explanation: Wonderful clinical thinking! Any sudden floppy weakness in a child must be treated as an AFP emergency with urgent reporting and samples.

question: Why is it important for Nigerian student nurses to know local waste management laws?

options.A: To advocate for proper safety resources and ensure hospital compliance
options.B: To design new electrical furnaces for the hospital engineering team
options.C: To take over the daily responsibilities of the municipal sanitation department
options.D: To handle the legal prosecution of commercial waste contractors directly

explanation: When you know the rules, you can spot safety hazards, ask management for the right protective gear, and keep your patients and colleagues safe!

question: When would a nurse researcher choose a qualitative design?

options.A: To test a specific drug dosage on a group of people
options.B: To prove cause and effect using large numerical samples
options.C: To quickly measure blood pressure across a large population
options.D: To explore the emotional details of a patient's illness

explanation: Great thinking! We use qualitative designs when we want rich, descriptive stories about human experiences instead of cold numbers.

question: What is the medical term for the natural weakening of the immune system that happens as people get older?

options.A: Immunosenescence
options.B: Hypersensitivity
options.C: Autoimmunity
options.D: Seroconversion

explanation: Well done! 'Immuno' relates to the immune system, and 'senescence' means growing older. Put them together and you get the age-related decline in immunity.

question: Which of these is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC)?

options.A: Male latex condom
options.B: Spermicidal foam
options.C: Intrauterine device
options.D: Oral contraceptive pill

explanation: An Intrauterine Device (IUD) is placed in the womb and provides protection for years, but can be removed anytime you want.

question: What often happens when healthcare team members communicate poorly with each other?

options.A: Better coordination of community support services
options.B: Medication errors and conflicting care instructions
options.C: Increased satisfaction among family caregivers
options.D: Faster recovery times for hospitalized patients

explanation: When health workers don't share updates, mistakes happen, and patients might get mixed-up advice or wrong treatments.

question: A mother brings in her infant who is very sleepy (lethargic) and vomiting everything she feeds her. According to IMCI, what do these signs mean?

options.A: Normal infant behavior during a mild growth spurt
options.B: Minor symptoms that can be treated at home with rest
options.C: Side effects of routine immunization that need no action
options.D: General danger signs requiring urgent hospital referral

explanation: Spot on! Lethargy and inability to keep fluids down are red-flag danger signs. They mean the baby needs emergency hospital care right away.

question: What is an early warning sign often reported by someone developing stomach cancer?

options.A: Fever and joint swelling
options.B: Sudden severe diarrhea
options.C: Bright red rectal bleeding
options.D: Early satiety and vague indigestion

explanation: You got it! Feeling full very quickly after eating a small meal (early satiety) along with mild, ongoing indigestion can be an early hint of stomach trouble.

question: A nursing student is counseling a new mother who fears that modern contraceptives cause permanent infertility. How should the student respond?

options.A: Agree with her and advise her to avoid all modern family planning
options.B: Provide accurate, gentle education to clear up the misconception
options.C: Tell her that her fears are silly and scold her for asking
options.D: Ignore her concern and force her to accept an implant

explanation: Nurses must address common myths with patience and factual evidence to help clients make informed healthcare choices. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of a strong focal point on a health education poster?

options.A: To make the poster look like a modern art painting
options.B: To hide the official logo of the sponsoring health organization
options.C: To immediately draw the viewer's attention to the core health topic
options.D: To use up empty white space at the bottom of the page

explanation: A great focal point grabs the eye instantly, making sure people catch the main health message even if they just glance at it quickly.

question: In aeromedical work, what does the safety acronym 'CRM' stand for?

options.A: Certified Rescue Medic
options.B: Crew Resource Management
options.C: Clinical Risk Method
options.D: Critical Respiratory Monitoring

explanation: You've got this! CRM is a fantastic aviation safety framework that encourages teamwork, clear communication, and shared problem-solving among everyone on board.

question: Why can extreme heat exposure during early pregnancy be risky for the developing baby?

options.A: It instantly changes the genetic blood type of the fetus
options.B: It triggers early puberty inside the womb
options.C: It causes the placenta to detach immediately on the first day
options.D: It can interfere with proper implantation and increase the risk of miscarriage

explanation: During early pregnancy, cells are dividing rapidly. High heat can disrupt this delicate process and put the pregnancy at risk. Every bit of knowledge gets you closer to exam success!

question: A clinic trains community health workers to give routine vaccines so nurses can focus on complex cases. What is this strategy called?

options.A: Currency devaluation
options.B: Task shifting
options.C: Out-of-pocket billing
options.D: Macroeconomic financing

explanation: Spot on! 'Task shifting' safely passes appropriate duties to trained support staff, helping the healthcare team work smarter and save costs.

question: What is the main goal of holding a post-clinical nursing care conference?

options.A: To clean and sterilize all the equipment used during the practical session
options.B: To reflect on clinical experiences, share insights, and discuss patient care outcomes
options.C: To allow the hospital director to review student attendance registers
options.D: To punish students who arrived late to the hospital ward shift

explanation: Post-clinical conferences are your chance to decompress, talk about what you saw on the ward, ask questions, and learn from your peers' experiences.

question: What is a key role of a nurse acting as a community champion for reproductive health?

options.A: Writing national health insurance budget laws
options.B: Replacing traditional village chiefs in council meetings
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical contraceptive drugs
options.D: Educating and advocating outside hospital walls

explanation: Community champions extend their reach into local spaces to educate populations and advocate for better health practices. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h6)

question: A patient with a history of A-fib suddenly has slurred speech and weakness on one side of the body. What is the likely cause?

options.A: A simple muscle cramp from low potassium
options.B: Temporary fatigue from standing up too fast
options.C: An allergic reaction to blood pressure pills
options.D: A stroke caused by a blood clot traveling to the brain

explanation: Classic stroke signs! Because of the A-fib, a clot likely formed in the heart, broke loose, traveled up to the brain, and blocked blood flow.

question: What is the main objective of secondary prevention?

options.A: Early detection and prompt treatment of a disease to stop its progress
options.B: Providing end-of-life comfort care for terminally ill cancer patients
options.C: Promoting nationwide policies against tobacco farming and importation
options.D: Eliminating all genetic mutations that run in family lineages

explanation: Spot on! Secondary prevention is about catching a disease early through screenings so we can treat it quickly before complications arise.

question: When is a therapeutic thoracocentesis performed?

options.A: When trapped fluid causes severe respiratory distress
options.B: When a patient requires daily routine blood tests
options.C: When doctors need to rule out a simple skin rash
options.D: When checking the strength of the heart valves

explanation: Therapeutic drainage is done to physically remove enough fluid to relieve pressure on the lungs and ease breathing. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h2)

question: Why do modern syringe drivers have security locks on their control panels?

options.A: To prevent the battery from falling out during transport
options.B: To automatically lock the infusion line if air bubbles appear
options.C: To prevent accidental changes to the rate by visitors or patients
options.D: To keep the internal clock set to the correct local time zone

explanation: Spot on! Security locks ensure that inquisitive fingers or accidental bumps don't change the prescribed medication speed.

question: Which part of the brain acts as our master biological clock?

options.A: The suprachiasmatic nucleus
options.B: The pituitary gland
options.C: The cerebellum
options.D: The medulla oblongata

explanation: Think of the suprachiasmatic nucleus as your body's personal timekeeper! Located in the hypothalamus, it takes in light signals from your eyes to keep your daily body rhythms on track.

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care for a cancer patient receiving end-of-life support?

options.A: Testing new experimental medication regimens
options.B: Maximizing comfort and maintaining dignity
options.C: Restoring normal nutritional and metabolic status
options.D: Aggressively treating the underlying tumor growth

explanation: At the end of life, our nursing focus shifts completely to surrounding the patient and family with comfort, peace, and dignity.

question: What is the very first thing you put on when wearing a full set of PPE?

options.A: Put on protective eyewear
options.B: Put on the surgical mask
options.C: Put on the isolation gown
options.D: Put on non-sterile gloves

explanation: That's correct! Always start with your gown, tying it securely to cover your uniform first. Your gloves always go on last, right over the gown sleeves.

question: What is the main focus of occupational therapy in subacute care?

options.A: Helping patients perform daily self-care tasks like dressing and bathing
options.B: Managing complex intravenous medications and wound dressings
options.C: Assessing nutritional intake and feeding tube placement needs
options.D: Restoring walking ability and lower body muscle strength

explanation: You nailed it! Occupational therapy focuses on helping clients get back to doing everyday activities independently.

question: What is the main difference between recording and reporting in the clinic?

options.A: Recording is writing down individual patient care, while reporting is summarizing data for higher health authorities.
options.B: Recording is done by doctors only while reporting is for nurses.
options.C: Recording uses electronic tablets while reporting uses paper only.
options.D: Recording happens once a year and reporting happens daily.

explanation: Think of recording as capturing what you do with one patient in front of you, while reporting is putting all those numbers together to send upstream so the government can plan public health! You've got this.

question: How is BCC different from standard, one-way health talks?

options.A: BCC focuses only on treating emergency trauma patients
options.B: BCC relies exclusively on television and radio broadcasts
options.C: BCC uses interactive dialogue instead of just giving information
options.D: BCC avoids talking directly with community members

explanation: You got it! While basic education just throws facts at people, BCC gets a conversation going so we can truly understand and address their concerns.

question: In healthcare finance, what does 'opportunity cost' mean?

options.A: The value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made
options.B: The total cost of operating a hospital for one calendar year
options.C: The penalty fee charged for mismanaged nursing budgets
options.D: The financial profit made from treating emergency patients

explanation: Opportunity cost is simply what you have to give up when you choose option A over option B. Every choice has a trade-off!

question: What should a nurse leader do if given an administrative order that breaks nursing ethics?

options.A: Refuse to comply and uphold professional ethical standards
options.B: Blame the junior staff if anything goes wrong
options.C: Resign immediately without reporting the issue
options.D: Follow the order blindly because administrators have absolute power

explanation: You're a patient advocate first! Professional ethics and patient safety always come before office orders that put people at risk.

question: Why is enteral tube feeding preferred over parenteral nutrition when the digestive tract works?

options.A: It delivers pure water without any dissolved nutrients
options.B: It requires no monitoring of blood glucose levels
options.C: It preserves gut function and protects the intestinal lining
options.D: It carries zero risk of infection or mechanical blockage

explanation: Using the gastrointestinal tract keeps the gut mucosa healthy and prevents bacterial translocation, making enteral feeding the safer choice. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h7)

question: What is the main benefit of regularly assessing immunization programs in primary health centers?

options.A: It helps locate groups with low vaccine uptake
options.B: It guarantees that outbreaks will never occur
options.C: It eliminates the need for keeping paper records
options.D: It replaces community health education talks

explanation: Assessing our services helps us spot gaps and find children who are missing out, so we know exactly where to direct our outreach efforts.

question: What is the main job of a medical-surgical nurse?

options.A: Managing administrative budgets for hospital wards and clinics
options.B: Caring for adult patients with various medical illnesses and surgical needs
options.C: Delivering emergency psychiatric interventions in crisis centers
options.D: Providing specialized surgical operations inside the operating theater

explanation: You'll see med-surg nursing everywhere in the hospital! It's all about looking after adults dealing with medical conditions or bouncing back from surgery. You've got this!

question: Why do we have to be extra careful when disposing of cytotoxic (chemotherapy) drugs?

options.A: Expired tablets turn into sweet-tasting candy that attracts children
options.B: These drugs instantly catch fire when exposed to ordinary air
options.C: Cytotoxic drugs are designed to destroy cells and can damage healthy tissue and genetic material
options.D: Chemotherapy drugs make the local soil extremely fertile for crops

explanation: Spot on! These medications are specially made to kill fast-growing cells, meaning they can harm healthy human tissue and our environment if carelessly thrown out.

question: What is a critical safety preparation for a child dependent on a mechanical ventilator at home?

options.A: Having a backup power source and manual resuscitation bag
options.B: Relying solely on the local utility company for power alerts
options.C: Disconnecting the alarm system to maintain household quiet
options.D: Keeping the child restricted to a bed at all times

explanation: Spot on! Power cuts happen unexpectedly, so families must always have backup power and a manual bag ready for emergencies. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard criterion for selecting an essential drug?

options.A: Bright packaging color and appealing flavor
options.B: High public health relevance
options.C: Proven clinical efficacy and safety
options.D: Acceptable cost-effectiveness

explanation: Aesthetic features like color and flavor do not determine whether a drug is medically essential for public health. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is a major workforce challenge currently facing the long-term care industry?

options.A: An overabundance of licensed nurses competing for very few open beds
options.B: Mandatory retirement ages that force nurses to leave the field early
options.C: Severe staff shortages and high burnout rates among nurses and aides
options.D: Strict laws prohibiting nurses from working in residential settings

explanation: It's no secret that long-term care can be tough. Low pay, heavy workloads, and physical demands mean keeping and recruiting enough nurses remains a major hurdle.

question: How can public health nurses use incidence data to check if an immunization campaign worked?

options.A: By calculating the average age of patients in the ward
options.B: By measuring the total money spent on medical supplies
options.C: By checking if the number of new infections drops over time
options.D: By counting the total number of hospital beds available

explanation: If a vaccination drive is successful, you should see the number of new infections (incidence) go way down. Awesome nursing logic!

question: Which cancer is the most common among Nigerian women?

options.A: Liver cancer
options.B: Breast cancer
options.C: Cervical cancer
options.D: Ovarian cancer

explanation: Breast cancer is recorded as the leading malignancy among women in Nigeria and globally. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h2)

question: A rural community suffers from a high rate of waterborne diseases like cholera. Besides treating sick patients, which action represents true intersectoral collaboration?

options.A: Asking nurses to work overtime shifts in the treatment tent
options.B: Increasing the price of local river water to discourage drinking it
options.C: Ordering more intravenous fluids from the central medical store
options.D: Partnering with public works and local leaders to build safe boreholes

explanation: Working with public works engineers addresses the environmental source of the problem rather than just treating the resulting illness. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the popular name of the form Nigerian health workers use to report suspected bad drug reactions?

options.A: The Red Hazard Card
options.B: The Green Incident Sheet
options.C: The Yellow Form
options.D: The Blue Prescription Pad

explanation: You nailed it! The Yellow Form is our trusty go-to paper tool in Nigerian hospitals for reporting suspected drug side effects.

question: What main body structures do the embryonic neural tube turn into?

options.A: Heart and major blood vessels
options.B: Skeletal muscles
options.C: Brain and spinal cord
options.D: Liver and pancreas

explanation: Spot on! The neural tube is the direct building block for the entire central nervous system—our brain and spinal cord.

question: What is the main goal of secondary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Enforcing broad national housing and environmental policies
options.B: Rehabilitating patients with long-term physical disabilities
options.C: Completely preventing the initial exposure to a pathogen
options.D: Early diagnosis and prompt treatment of existing disease

explanation: Secondary prevention is all about catching health issues early through screening so we can treat them before they get worse.

question: How do sudden altitude changes during an air medical evacuation affect a patient?

options.A: They instantly lower the patient's core body temperature
options.B: They prevent intravenous pumps from delivering fluids
options.C: They completely eliminate the risk of internal bleeding
options.D: They cause trapped gases inside body cavities to expand

explanation: As the plane climbs and air pressure drops, any trapped air inside the body—like in the gut or middle ear—expands just like a bag of chips at high altitude!

question: Which sign shows mental fatigue in neurasthenia?

options.A: Sudden loss of consciousness
options.B: Uncontrollable muscle twitching
options.C: Poor memory and reduced concentration
options.D: Auditory and visual hallucinations

explanation: Great try! Mental tiredness directly affects your brain's ability to focus and remember things. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: What is the main job of a mechanical ventilator in the hospital ward?

options.A: To support or replace spontaneous breathing
options.B: To permanently eliminate the need for oxygen therapy
options.C: To cure underlying pulmonary infections
options.D: To lower systemic blood pressure safely

explanation: Think of the ventilator as an extra pair of lungs for patients who are too tired or sick to breathe well on their own. It takes over or helps out until they recover!

question: Why are exclusion criteria inside a standing order just as important as inclusion criteria?

options.A: They reduce the amount of paperwork the nurse needs to fill out at the end of the shift
options.B: They guarantee that the patient will recover without needing any follow-up visits
options.C: They tell the pharmacist how many tablets of each medication to dispense
options.D: They help identify warning signs that mean the patient is too sick for routine protocol treatment

explanation: Exclusion criteria flag danger signs or complications that require immediate referral rather than standard clinic treatment. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h4)

question: What is the main reason teenagers often avoid seeking healthcare for sensitive personal issues?

options.A: Preference for traditional herbal remedies only
options.B: Fear of parents or community members finding out
options.C: A lack of interest in personal hygiene
options.D: The high cost of prescription eyeglasses

explanation: Without guaranteed privacy, teens worry about gossip and judgment from adults they know in the community. Privacy builds trust!

question: What does a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) tell you?

options.A: The exact number of doses remaining inside the glass vial
options.B: Whether heat exposure has damaged the vaccine's potency
options.C: Whether the vaccine container has been contaminated with bacteria
options.D: The precise manufacturing date printed on the cardboard box

explanation: Think of the VVM as a heat-watchdog! It changes color when exposed to too much heat, letting you know if the vaccine is still safe to use.

question: An elderly patient taking many unnecessary drugs is most at risk for which problem?

options.A: Rapid increase in daily physical activity
options.B: Sudden improvement in physical endurance
options.C: Severe adverse drug reactions and toxicity
options.D: Complete immunity to all common infections

explanation: Older adults process drugs more slowly, making them highly vulnerable to side effects and dangerous drug interactions. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h4)

question: A nurse is getting ready to apply a new fentanyl pain patch to a patient. What important step must be done first?

options.A: Cover the new patch completely with airtight plastic wrap
options.B: Scrub the application site aggressively with surgical soap
options.C: Remove the previous transdermal patch from the patient's skin
options.D: Warm the new patch over a flame to activate the chemicals

explanation: Always take off the old patch before putting on a new one! Leaving the old patch on can cause a dangerous, life-threatening drug overdose.

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for patients in skin traction?

options.A: Mental fatigue prevents the patient from eating hospital meals
options.B: Anxious patients have higher rates of bone infection than calm ones
options.C: Psychological stress stops the traction weights from pulling correctly
options.D: Bed confinement and restricted movement cause significant anxiety and frustration

explanation: Being stuck flat in one position is tough on the mind as well as the body. A kind word and clear communication go a long way in nursing care!

question: Where do the bones of your skull and jaw mostly come from during early development?

options.A: Visceral endoderm
options.B: Neural crest cells
options.C: Pelvic mesoderm
options.D: Cardiac jelly

explanation: Think of neural crest cells as great travelers—they migrate forward into the head region early on to form your face and skull bones!

question: A discharged patient with a spinal injury cannot afford their wheelchair or follow-up therapy. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Buy the expensive equipment with personal salary
options.B: Tell them to stop all medications immediately
options.C: Say financial issues are none of nursing's business
options.D: Refer the patient to medical social services for financial counseling and support

explanation: You don't have to pay out of your own pocket! Connecting the patient to the medical social work department is the right professional step to bridge that gap.

question: Why do we irrigate a fresh bite wound with plenty of sterile fluid?

options.A: To dissolve all the surrounding dead skin cells
options.B: To physically wash away bacteria and loose debris
options.C: To permanently freeze the nerve endings to stop pain
options.D: To stimulate rapid production of new blood cells

explanation: Using fluid force is one of our best nursing tools to physically rinse out contaminating microbes and dirt left behind by the bite.

question: Why shouldn't a nurse manager rely only on money and bonuses to keep staff happy long-term?

options.A: Pay raises are illegal in most government-owned healthcare facilities
options.B: Extrinsic rewards always decrease the total quality of patient care
options.C: Financial bonuses do not sustain long-term engagement like internal professional drivers do
options.D: Nurses generally dislike receiving extra money for their hard work

explanation: While cash bonuses are nice, they don't replace the deep need for respect, growth, and purpose. True, lasting job satisfaction comes from feeling valued inside.

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take after sustaining an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and water
options.B: Fill out an incident report form for the manager
options.C: Squeeze the finger tightly to push out old blood
options.D: Apply an antiseptic iodine ointment and a bandage

explanation: Immediate washing reduces the viral or bacterial load introduced at the puncture site before it enters the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why do teenage girls need more daily iron in their diet than younger children do?

options.A: To prevent soft bones from a lack of sunlight
options.B: To support monthly period blood loss and growing muscles
options.C: To maintain normal skin color and elasticity
options.D: To help digest heavy local meals easily

explanation: You nailed it! Monthly periods and rapid physical growth use up iron quickly, so eating more iron-rich foods helps prevent anemia.

question: You see chemo leaking into the skin around an IV site. What is your very first action?

options.A: Slow down the infusion pump to a trickle
options.B: Apply a firm pressure bandage over the site
options.C: Stop the infusion and disconnect the tubing
options.D: Flush the IV line with normal saline

explanation: Action! Stop it immediately. Stopping the flow right away limits how much harmful drug gets into the surrounding skin tissue.

question: Why is giving plenty of fluids a top nursing priority during a sickle cell pain crisis?

options.A: It decreases blood viscosity, helping sickled cells flow through small vessels
options.B: It prevents the kidneys from filtering out necessary pain medications
options.C: It directly stops the bone marrow from producing abnormal haemoglobin S
options.D: It replaces the white blood cells that are lost during a hemolytic attack

explanation: Hydration is key! Fluids thin out the blood (reduces viscosity), making it much easier for those sticky cells to move through tight blood vessels.

question: Which tocolytic drug is usually avoided past 32 weeks because it can affect the baby's heart circulation?

options.A: Indomethacin
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Terbutaline
options.D: Nifedipine

explanation: Indomethacin is a prostaglandin blocker, but we have to be careful using it late in pregnancy so it doesn't cause early closure of the baby's ductus arteriosus. Excellent pharmacological safety!

question: What is widely considered the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in a hospital?

options.A: Wearing heavy utility gloves all day
options.B: Spraying chemical disinfectants on walls
options.C: Keeping all windows wide open
options.D: Consistent and proper hand hygiene

explanation: Good old handwashing (or using an alcohol rub) is your superpower. It stops germs dead in their tracks before they reach you or your next patient.

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC)?

options.A: To reduce maternal illness and death from abortion complications
options.B: To provide permanent sterilization to all female patients
options.C: To investigate the legal circumstances of a pregnancy loss
options.D: To promote mandatory reporting of all spontaneous miscarriages

explanation: Great job! PAC is all about saving lives and treating any physical or emotional issues after a pregnancy loss so the patient can recover safely.

question: An unconscious motor vehicle crash victim is brought into the emergency room making gurgling noises. What is the immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Check the patient's blood glucose level immediately
options.B: Start an intravenous line to administer pain medication
options.C: Clear and secure the airway while protecting the neck
options.D: Ask the family members how the accident happened

explanation: Airway clearance is always the first step in trauma resuscitation, especially when gurgling indicates fluid or obstruction in an unconscious patient. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h3)

question: What is the main job of the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: Transmitting sensory signals from the skin
options.B: Regulating involuntary body functions
options.C: Processing conscious thought and memory
options.D: Controlling voluntary skeletal muscles

explanation: Think of the autonomic system as your body's autopilot. It takes care of internal organs and smooth muscles automatically so you don't have to consciously tell your heart to beat or your food to digest!

question: What does the glycemic index (GI) measure about a carbohydrate food?

options.A: The amount of sodium added during processing
options.B: How much total fiber is in the serving
options.C: How fast and high it raises blood sugar
options.D: The exact number of calories it contains

explanation: The glycemic index ranks foods by their speed and intensity in raising blood glucose levels. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h3)

question: Why do private healthcare facilities tend to avoid opening branches in poor rural communities?

options.A: Governments forbid private clinics in rural zones
options.B: The expected financial return is too low
options.C: Rural residents never experience health problems
options.D: Staff refuse to live outside major cities

explanation: Profit-driven enterprises invest where patients have the financial means to pay for services, leading to rural medical deserts. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h5)

question: If you delegate a routine task to a nursing assistant as a registered nurse, who still holds the ultimate legal responsibility?

options.A: The hospital ward manager on duty
options.B: The nursing assistant who performed the task
options.C: The registered nurse who made the delegation
options.D: The physician in charge of the patient

explanation: Remember this rule: you can delegate tasks, but you can never delegate ultimate accountability. As the RN, you supervise and check the final outcome!

question: Why must patient assessment in palliative care be an ongoing, continuous process?

options.A: Because terminal illnesses and symptom experiences change rapidly over time
options.B: Because laboratory values fluctuate constantly during end-of-life care
options.C: Because hospital regulations require daily documentation updates
options.D: Because family members frequently change their minds about treatment

explanation: As serious illnesses progress, new symptoms pop up and emotional states shift. Constant checking and reassessing help us adjust care to keep the patient as comfortable as possible. Keep shining!

question: What is the main goal of medical treatment for Pick's disease?

options.A: Restoring lost brain tissue in the frontal lobe
options.B: Reversing the underlying cellular tau accumulation
options.C: Curing the primary neurodegenerative process
options.D: Managing behavioral symptoms and improving comfort

explanation: Since we can't cure or reverse the disease yet, our nursing care focuses on keeping the patient comfortable, calm, and managing tough behavioral symptoms.

question: Which group of mental health conditions features overwhelming fear and ongoing distress?

options.A: Depressive and Bipolar Disorders
options.B: Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorders
options.C: Anxiety and Trauma-Related Disorders
options.D: Personality Disorders

explanation: These disorders are tied to persistent fear, constant high alert, and stress linked to difficult life events. Keep building that clinical vocabulary!

question: Which blood vessel brings oxygen-rich blood *back* from the placenta to the baby?

options.A: Spiral artery
options.B: Endometrial vein
options.C: Umbilical vein
options.D: Umbilical artery

explanation: A little clinical trick: just like veins in our body normally carry blood back to the heart, the umbilical *vein* carries fresh, oxygenated blood from the placenta to the baby. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why should you quickly check on your patient right before you carry out a planned intervention?

options.A: To confirm that the planned action is still safe and necessary for them right now
options.B: To rewrite the entire medical diagnosis from the beginning
options.C: To make sure the physician is standing nearby to supervise the nursing care
options.D: To ensure that all hospital equipment has been paid for in advance

explanation: Patients change fast! What was a great plan an hour ago might need tweaking if their condition shifts. Always assess before you act.

question: How do recurring illnesses like malaria lead to childhood malnutrition?

options.A: By directly destroying the child's bone marrow and skeleton
options.B: By changing the color of breast milk in the mother's body
options.C: By forcing the child to sleep longer hours during the day
options.D: By increasing nutrient demand while reducing the child's appetite

explanation: Fever and sickness make the body burn more energy, but sick kids usually don't want to eat. That combination leads straight to weight loss.

question: Why must you always ask patients about any herbal remedies they take alongside prescription drugs?

options.A: Some herbs can dangerously alter the effects of prescribed medications
options.B: Traditional plants always neutralize standard hospital equipment
options.C: Herbal remedies are illegal to consume in any home care setting
options.D: Doctors refuse to document any natural products in the chart

explanation: Spot on! Herbs are active substances. Mixing them with hospital drugs can accidentally boost or block the medication, causing dangerous side effects.

question: What is the very first step in the management control process?

options.A: Taking corrective action steps
options.B: Comparing results against targets
options.C: Measuring actual work performance
options.D: Establishing performance standards

explanation: Before you can measure or fix anything, you need to set clear guidelines so everyone knows what good performance looks like!

question: Which little flap of tissue automatically covers your windpipe when you swallow, keeping food out of your lungs?

options.A: The epiglottis
options.B: The uvula
options.C: The lower esophageal sphincter
options.D: The soft palate

explanation: Think of the epiglottis as a trapdoor! When you swallow, it folds down over your larynx and trachea to block food and drinks from taking a wrong turn into your lungs.

question: A patient recovering from serum sickness complains of stiff, aching joints. Which nursing action is best?

options.A: Apply ice packs to the joints for twenty minutes every hour
options.B: Massage the inflamed joint firmly to break up the immune complexes
options.C: Keep the affected limbs strictly immobilized in a rigid splint
options.D: Encourage gentle range-of-motion exercises as tolerated

explanation: Gentle movement is wonderful here; it keeps the joints from locking up while giving the tissues space to heal comfortably.

question: Which four elements form the main building blocks of most nutrients in our diet?

options.A: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen
options.B: Phosphorus, sulfur, chlorine, and magnesium
options.C: Calcium, iron, sodium, and potassium
options.D: Copper, zinc, iodine, and manganese

explanation: Spot on! These four simple elements form the chemical backbone of the carbohydrates, fats, proteins, and nucleic acids we eat every day.

question: What was the first major antipsychotic medication discovered in the 1950s?

options.A: Lithium carbonate
options.B: Diazepam
options.C: Chlorpromazine
options.D: Fluoxetine

explanation: Chlorpromazine was the pioneering antipsychotic drug that revolutionized the medical management of severe psychiatric disorders. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h5)

question: A clinic team has ten great ideas but only enough time to test one. What should they do first?

options.A: Implement all ten ideas simultaneously to save time
options.B: Discard all ideas and keep the current routine unchanged
options.C: Use an impact-versus-effort matrix to filter and prioritize the ideas
options.D: Pick the longest and most expensive idea to look impressive

explanation: A prioritization matrix simply helps you weigh which idea will give the best results with a realistic amount of effort. Work smarter, not harder!

question: What is the core focus of the modern field called nutrigenomics?

options.A: How to grow crops without using water
options.B: How to eliminate all fats from human diets
options.C: How to manufacture artificial synthetic vitamins
options.D: How food and nutrients interact with human genes

explanation: Brilliant! Nutrigenomics looks at the cool science of how your unique genetic makeup changes the way your body responds to the food you eat.

question: How can you make sure your midwifery kit is always ready for an emergency call?

options.A: By washing the outside canvas bag once a year
options.B: By keeping the bag tightly locked until an emergency happens
options.C: By swapping metal tools for plastic toys to stay light
options.D: By checking inventory and expiry dates after every single use

explanation: Restocking and checking dates right after a case means you will never open your bag during an emergency only to find something expired or missing!

question: When do you need to use strict surgical asepsis instead of everyday medical asepsis?

options.A: Putting on clean gloves to empty a full bedpan
options.B: Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter into the bladder
options.C: Performing routine hand hygiene before feeding a patient
options.D: Wiping down a patient's bedside table with a disinfectant

explanation: Whenever you enter a sterile body tract like the bladder, you need absolute sterile technique to keep bacteria out. You've got this!

question: Where should the money come from to pay for drugs given out under an exemption policy?

options.A: Extra fees charged secretly to other ordinary patients
options.B: Deductions taken directly from the personal salaries of nurses
options.C: Dedicated external subsidy pools, grants, or hospital subventions
options.D: Donations collected from patients waiting in the outpatient queue

explanation: External funds or hospital subventions must reimburse the DRF account so that providing free care to the poor doesn't ruin the pharmacy stock.

question: What is an example of closed-loop communication during a resuscitation?

options.A: Calling out for extra help over the hospital public address system
options.B: Repeating an order back to the leader to confirm it was heard and understood
options.C: Nodding your head silently when the doctor walks into the room
options.D: Writing down all medications on a paper chart after the code ends

explanation: Closed-loop communication prevents dangerous mistakes by ensuring every order is clearly acknowledged and verified. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h8)

question: What does 'tidaling' mean in the water seal chamber?
