options.C: To verify that the patient is maintaining adequate daily hydration
options.D: To track how well the liver is producing albumin for the kidneys

explanation: These medications can occasionally slow down bone marrow activity. Regular blood counts help us catch any drops in white or red blood cells early on.

question: Why is assigning specific responsibilities crucial in a healthcare plan?

options.A: It makes it easier to punish workers when they make mistakes.
options.B: It ensures that doctors do all the work instead of nurses.
options.C: If a task belongs to everyone, nobody will actually do it.
options.D: Hospital accreditation boards require alphabetical staff lists.

explanation: Clear accountability ensures every duty has a designated owner who is responsible for seeing it through to the end.

question: A student gets severe eye strain and sleepiness during afternoon lectures in a room with no windows. What is the most likely physical cause?

options.A: Inadequate lighting
options.B: Poor acoustic design
options.C: Uncomfortable desk ergonomics
options.D: High social anxiety

explanation: Bad lighting in windowless rooms forces your eyes to work much harder, directly causing strain and tiredness. Good lighting makes a huge difference!

question: What is the main goal of continuous bladder irrigation (CBI) after prostate surgery?

options.A: To deliver strong antibiotic drugs directly to the prostate tissue
options.B: To permanently shrink any remaining benign prostate cells
options.C: To measure the exact daily hormonal output of the testes
options.D: To prevent blood clot retention and keep the catheter open

explanation: After surgery, bleeding can form clots that block the catheter. CBI flushes fluid in and out continuously to keep everything clear and flowing!

question: What is the main job of the myelin covering wrapped around a nerve fiber?

options.A: To manufacture neurotransmitters for the synapse
options.B: To anchor the neuron firmly to surrounding bone
options.C: To increase the speed of nerve impulse conduction
options.D: To provide a steady supply of oxygen to the neuron

explanation: Well done! Myelin acts like plastic insulation on an electrical wire, helping nerve signals travel much faster.

question: Why do many Nigerian patients choose private health facilities even though they must pay cash out of pocket?

options.A: They often perceive private care to have better quality and shorter waiting times
options.B: Private hospitals offer free medications to every registered citizen
options.C: Private clinics are entirely subsidized by federal government revenue
options.D: The law forbids them from visiting public hospitals for minor illnesses

explanation: Frustration with long queues and drug stockouts in public hospitals drives many citizens to private clinics, cost notwithstanding. It's a clear indicator of systemic challenges!

question: During a digestive check, which physical sign is best for quickly spotting dehydration?

options.A: Moisture of the oral mucous membranes
options.B: The presence of minor scars on the skin
options.C: The temperature of the lower legs
options.D: The exact color of the client's hair

explanation: Checking inside the mouth! Dry or sticky gums and tongue are quick, reliable signs that a patient is losing too much fluid from vomiting or diarrhea.

question: In history, why did many Nigerian communities use facial marks?

options.A: To hide physical facial injuries
options.B: To show ethnic identity and lineage
options.C: To treat severe bacterial infections
options.D: To prevent normal childhood growth

explanation: Spot on! Traditional facial marks acted like a visual passport to show a person's hometown, family roots, and community heritage.

question: Why is daily movement so important for patients who are stuck on bed rest?

options.A: It cures underlying chronic medical conditions completely
options.B: It prevents the loss of muscle strength and joint flexibility
options.C: It guarantees a shorter hospital stay for every patient
options.D: It eliminates the need for pain medication administration

explanation: Lying in bed all day makes the body weak very quickly. Simple daily movements stop muscles from wasting away and keep joints moving smoothly.

question: What is the main purpose of patient categorization in home health care?

options.A: To group individuals based on their specific health needs and care type
options.B: To eliminate the need for home visits by professional nurses
options.C: To decide which patients must return to the hospital immediately
options.D: To reduce the total number of medications a patient takes daily

explanation: Categorizing patients allows nurses to understand unique care requirements and plan appropriate interventions for each person. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h1)

question: Six hours after delivery, a mom feels dizzy. You check and find her uterus is soft (boggy) and pushed to the right. What is your immediate nursing action?

options.A: Prepare the patient for immediate major surgery
options.B: Massage the uterine fundus until firm and encourage bladder emptying
options.C: Administer oral pain relievers and tell her to sleep
options.D: Check her blood glucose level and offer juice

explanation: A boggy uterus means it's relaxing and bleeding could start! Massaging it helps it contract, and getting her to empty her bladder will stop it from being pushed out of place.

question: An older patient only eats tea and bread every day. What is the best next step for the nurse?

options.A: Collaborate with a dietitian to plan nutrient-dense meals and snacks
options.B: Scold the patient for having poor eating habits
options.C: Document that the patient has perfect nutritional status
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately since they are eating something

explanation: You're a natural! Once you spot a nutritional gap, teaming up with a dietitian is the best way to help the patient eat healthier.

question: What is the main goal of presenting research results in nursing?

options.A: To show off complex mathematical calculations
options.B: To hide missing values and recording errors
options.C: To tell an honest and accurate story about the data
options.D: To prove that the hypothesis was always correct

explanation: The primary purpose of data presentation is to clearly and honestly communicate what the research findings reveal to other professionals. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is improvisation a valuable skill for a nursing educator working in a resource-limited setting?

options.A: It guarantees that students will pass board exams on the first try
options.B: It replaces the need for clinical hospital postings
options.C: It is always superior to factory-made medical equipment
options.D: It overcomes financial shortages without sacrificing student learning

explanation: Improvisation allows educators to deliver practical, high-quality lessons even when funds for buying commercial teaching aids are limited. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h6)

question: Which cranial nerve carries hearing and balance messages from the ear to the brain?

options.A: Cranial nerve VIII
options.B: Cranial nerve V
options.C: Cranial nerve II
options.D: Cranial nerve X

explanation: Cranial nerve VIII is also known as the vestibulocochlear nerve—combining balance (vestibule) and hearing (cochlea) into one pathway!

question: Why do many men unknowingly spread STIs to their partners?

options.A: They only transmit infections during the winter months
options.B: They refuse to take oral medications prescribed by nurses
options.C: They develop immediate immunity that masks active laboratory results
options.D: They frequently harbour asymptomatic infections without realising it

explanation: Many guys walk around feeling totally fine with zero symptoms (asymptomatic), which is why testing is so important even when someone feels healthy!

question: What level of technique is normally used when changing chronic wound dressings at home?

options.A: Clean technique
options.B: Surgical sterility
options.C: Chemical disinfection only
options.D: Complete germ-free isolation

explanation: For routine home care, clean technique is the standard! It relies on solid hand hygiene and clean tools rather than trying to keep things operating-room sterile.

question: What is a major duty of a medical social worker in a rehab setting?

options.A: Doing physical strength exercises with recovering patients
options.B: Conducting formal swallow studies for dysphagia patients
options.C: Prescribing pain medications and muscle relaxants
options.D: Checking home safety and connecting families to helpful resources

explanation: Social workers are fantastic advocates! They look at home environments and link families with community support, equipment, and funding.

question: A heavy rainstorm destroys homes in a rural village. Which local group is in the best position to take immediate action first?

options.A: International Red Cross headquarters abroad
options.B: The National Assembly legislative committee
options.C: The Federal Ministry of Aviation
options.D: Local Emergency Management Committees

explanation: Local committees are right there in the community, making them the fastest first responders on the ground before higher agencies arrive. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h3)

question: Why should nurses approach patient non-compliance with empathy instead of anger?

options.A: Because pharmaceutical companies require nurses to defend poor patient habits
options.B: Because judgmental attitudes automatically make patients immune to prescription drugs
options.C: Because non-compliance is usually driven by complex underlying barriers rather than simple defiance
options.D: Because hospital policies prohibit nurses from correcting patients who miss doses

explanation: Spot on! When we look past the surface, we find real struggles like high costs or confusion—not stubbornness.

question: What is the primary meaning of women empowerment in a healthcare context?

options.A: Gaining control and the ability to make choices about health and life
options.B: Eliminating the need for medical practitioners in rural villages
options.C: Taking over leadership roles exclusively in hospital management boards
options.D: Ensuring women work exclusively outside the home environment

explanation: Empowerment centers on gaining personal autonomy and the capacity to make vital decisions regarding one's health and well-being. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h1)

question: What is the main focus of 'andragogy'?

options.A: Managing hospital budgets
options.B: Educating pediatric patients
options.C: Teaching adult learners
options.D: Conducting laboratory research

explanation: Think of andragogy as the art and science of helping adults learn—people like you, who want to know the 'why' behind what they study!

question: Besides physical safety, what else helps create a healing ward environment?

options.A: Playing loud music to keep patients awake during the day
options.B: Keeping the lights at maximum brightness twenty-four hours a day
options.C: Allowing visitors to stay without any time limits
options.D: Reducing noise and addressing patient grievances promptly

explanation: You've got this! Healing isn't just physical—lowering stress by keeping noise down and listening to patient complaints makes a huge difference.

question: What is the big danger of using a sample size that is too small?

options.A: Patients will complain about excessive blood draws and paperwork
options.B: The study may miss important clinical findings and show a false negative
options.C: The hospital ethics committee will automatically ban future studies
options.D: The researchers will spend too much money buying medical supplies

explanation: Spot on! If your sample is too tiny, your study won't have enough muscle to spot a real breakthrough, making it look like nothing happened.

question: When mistakes happen in the clinic, what is usually the real root cause?

options.A: Flawed system designs interacting with human limits
options.B: Poor physical fitness and lack of sleep
options.C: A lack of basic nursing education among staff
options.D: Intentional negligence by individual healthcare workers

explanation: You're doing great! Remember that most clinical errors happen because the work environment and tools don't properly support natural human limits—not because nurses are careless.

question: What is the primary clinical objective of granting occasional leave to a psychiatric patient?

options.A: To permanently transfer legal responsibility to the family
options.B: To test if the patient can survive without food
options.C: To maintain family ties and test reality on a short-term basis
options.D: To clear up hospital beds for emergency surgical admissions

explanation: Short leaves are wonderful for keeping family bonds strong and letting nurses observe how the patient copes with a brief change in scenery.

question: What are early warning signs of a psychiatric relapse?

options.A: Immediate physical healing of a broken bone
options.B: Winning an award at work or school
options.C: Sudden complete recovery and happiness
options.D: Subtle changes like trouble sleeping, irritability, and withdrawing from others

explanation: Early warning signs are small behavioral or emotional shifts that appear before a major crisis occurs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why does the law make reporting certain infectious diseases compulsory for health workers?

options.A: To allow early government action to stop epidemics from spreading
options.B: To increase the financial taxes collected from local hospitals
options.C: To punish patients who contract preventable bacterial infections
options.D: To create extra paperwork for overworked nursing staff

explanation: Exactly! Quick reporting gives public health teams the heads-up they need to step in and contain an outbreak before it gets out of hand.

question: Why does obstetric fistula often cause women to face social isolation in their communities?

options.A: Patients lose their ability to speak after the injury
options.B: Continuous incontinence leads to severe social stigma and shame
options.C: Government laws require isolation of all surgical patients
options.D: Traditional healers forbid them from leaving their homes

explanation: Because of constant leaking of urine or stool, affected women often face heartbreaking stigma and misunderstanding from their communities. As nurses, our empathy and care are crucial in supporting and healing them.

question: A patient diagnosed with a serious illness insists the lab made a mistake and they are completely fine. What defense mechanism is this?

options.A: Regression
options.B: Intellectualization
options.C: Denial
options.D: Sublimation

explanation: Denial is our mind's way of protecting us by refusing to accept a painful or scary truth until we are ready to process it. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h6)

question: You want to find out which months malaria cases peak and food is scarcest in a farming village. Which tool should you use?

options.A: A biometric blood test
options.B: A structural house blueprint
options.C: A hospital budget ledger
options.D: A seasonal calendar

explanation: Spot on! Seasonal calendars let you visually map out changes across the year, tracking things like disease cycles and food supply.

question: A patient says her periods always arrive every 28 days, last 5 days, and have a moderate flow. What is your best initial nursing action?

options.A: Document this as a normal finding in her chart
options.B: Instruct her to start taking oral contraceptives
options.C: Order emergency hormone blood tests
options.D: Refer her immediately to a gynecological surgeon

explanation: A classic 28-day cycle with moderate flow is textbook normal! No interventions or emergency tests are needed—just a clean, accurate chart entry.

question: Why are newborn babies born with soft spots and flexible skull bones?

options.A: To allow the skull bones to overlap during birth and accommodate rapid brain growth
options.B: To let the cerebrospinal fluid drain easily through the scalp tissues
options.C: To prevent the brain from expanding too quickly before walking begins
options.D: To keep the infant's head cool during high fevers in the first year

explanation: Spot on! That flexibility helps the baby's head squeeze safely through the birth canal and gives the brain plenty of room to grow fast afterwards.

question: What age threshold is generally used to define a teenage bride?

options.A: Marriage before the onset of menarche
options.B: Marriage before the sixteenth birthday
options.C: Any marriage occurring while in secondary school
options.D: Marriage before the eighteenth birthday

explanation: Globally, a teenage bride is defined as any young girl who gets married before turning 18. Spotting this helps nurses identify vulnerable teens early!

question: What is the best position for a patient during a thoracocentesis?

options.A: Lying flat on their stomach with the head turned to the side
options.B: Lying flat on their back with arms straight down
options.C: Sitting upright and leaning forward over a bedside table
options.D: Standing upright against a rigid wall with eyes closed

explanation: This posture widens the spaces between the ribs, making it safer and easier to insert the needle. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h3)

question: Which antibody class is mostly found in body secretions like breast milk and saliva?

options.A: IgD
options.B: IgG
options.C: IgA
options.D: IgE

explanation: Secretory IgA is our body's frontline defender in wet areas! It guards mucosal linings in our respiratory and digestive tracts, and is proudly passed to babies through breast milk.

question: How was the role of a nurse different in early asylum days compared to modern nursing?

options.A: Nurses focused exclusively on intensive individual psychotherapy
options.B: Nurses were primarily responsible for prescribing antipsychotic medications
options.C: Nurses spent most of their time running community outreach clinics
options.D: Nurses functioned mainly as guards focused on physical containment and order

explanation: Correct! Back then, security came before healing, so nurses spent a lot of their time managing locked doors and enforcing physical control instead of therapeutic care.

question: Why is it better to help an older patient sit in a chair for meals instead of keeping them flat in bed?

options.A: It saves the nursing staff time during meal distribution
options.B: It is a strict hospital rule with no clinical reasoning behind it
options.C: It completely cures chronic joint arthritis in the legs
options.D: It prevents muscle deconditioning and improves digestion and alertness

explanation: Well done! Sitting upright helps them swallow safely, digests food better, and keeps them awake and alert.

question: Which bones make up the sides and roof of a baby's skull?

options.A: Frontal bones
options.B: Occipital bones
options.C: Parietal bones
options.D: Temporal bones

explanation: You've got this! The two large parietal bones cover the upper sides of the head and do the heavy lifting when the skull compresses during birth.

question: What is the main reason a nurse schedules serial ultrasounds for a pregnant client with sickle cell disease?

options.A: To check if the maternal pelvis is widening properly
options.B: To measure the exact volume of maternal amniotic fluid daily
options.C: To determine the exact genetic subtype of the fetus
options.D: To monitor fetal growth and screen for fetal anemia

explanation: You're doing great! Regular scans help us check how well the baby is growing and keep an eye out for fetal anemia.
